answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making admission a slow, costly rite rather than an instant claim. Every new identity must plant a cedar: a bond locked for six epochs, a public log entry, and ten countersigned tasks completed under reviewers drawn from outside its cluster. A zephyr of fresh keys cannot shortcut the queue, because each key needs its own planting and its own countersignatures. Failed audits slash the bond and send the account to a tundra of zero weight.
